What happened

Four held articles never aired on their focus day

Focus routing released 0 articles and held 4. Two were held for "The Living World" and two for "Maker & Repair", with target release dates of 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-22. None of the four reached an episode on this run. They remain in the queue for their focus days, so the cost to listeners tonight was zero stories from those focus slots, and the cost to the cycle is that the Maker & Repair and Living World weeks will carry a smaller pool than the schedule assumes.

The forestry focus week (cycle week 2 of 4) released nothing from the focus routing itself, so the theme and local material carried the whole episode. Check whether the routing should release a minimum count when the focus day is not the current one.

Eighteen roundup stories kept, twenty-three cut, two deep dives

The roundup pool held 18 stories: 15 theme and 3 local. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) dropped 23 from the pool, so the aired segment covered a fraction of what was curated. By design, the cut stories stay eligible for a later day. The deep dive pair was the Quesnel curtailment coverage, with the lead set to local under the Cariboo heading, which is where the debate question on who counts as affected by the curtailment came from.

Of 5 local stories available, 3 aired, and the roundup opened on local material. Citation alignment in the roundup matched 11 of 18, while both deep-dive citations matched. The gap in the roundup is the one to watch: 7 unmatched citations in a segment of 15 planned pairs means some spoken claims are not tied to a source the listener can find.

Change: review the roundup citation matching in the script-assembly step, since 11 of 18 is the weakest number on the page.

The first draft came in 753 words short and the expand pass fixed it

The first draft ran 2547 words against a target of 3400. It was sent back for one expand pass and shipped at 3223 words, which is still under target. Under the rule that a thin day is intended and only matters against SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS, this run is acceptable, but the gap shows the pool was not deep enough to fill the target without the expand pass. Casey's share of the deep-dive words was 48%, and the Casey-to-Riley voice ratio was 0.92, so the two voices stayed close to balanced.

Two TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicted. Each was retried once, and both retries stayed short. The longer take of each was kept, so no words were dropped from the audio, though the two takes may have been clipped at the source.

Change: if the expand pass is the regular fix for thin days, raise the default pool size so the first draft reaches target without a second pass.

▲
Shipped, needs a look4 things to look at before tomorrow's run.

What to do

  1. render/music-fallback fell back. Search the run log for Degraded 'render/music-fallback' and decide whether the fallback is acceptable or the cause needs fixing.
    degrade() row: script did not parse into welcome/news/deep-dive — episode rendered without music beds or section structure
  2. script/kagi-extract fell back. Search the run log for Degraded 'script/kagi-extract' and decide whether the fallback is acceptable or the cause needs fixing.
    degrade() row: Kagi Extract reply matched no page for 2 of 2 URLs sent
  3. Investigate.
    2 local stor(ies) in the pool, 1 aired, roundup opened local: no Recurring: pending for the roadmap, seen 1 night.
  4. The deep dive ran on one source with on-theme candidates unused. Read the Cariboo pick line in the run log and the candidates it passed over.
    the deep dive aired on one source while 32 on-theme candidate(s) went unused

What happened

Two segments fell back to a degraded render, and the script never parsed into sections

The script step produced a draft, but the segment parser could not split it into welcome, news and deep-dive, so the render fell back to TTS-only mode. The episode went out without music beds or section structure. The parse warning reads "Segment parsing failed - falling back to TTS-only mode", and the render degradation carries the same cause. The listener gets a continuous spoken track with no transitions between the roundup and the deep dive.

Alongside this, the Kagi Extract step matched no page for 2 of 2 URLs sent, so the script had no extracted article text for either of those sources. Set the parse failure next to the extract failure and the pattern is that the script stage is degrading in two places at once. Check the segment delimiters in the script prompt and the Kagi Extract request format before the next run.

The roundup aired one of two local stories, and the deep dive is the local one

The roundup pool held 18 stories, 17 on theme and 1 local, and the airtime budget cut 42 from the pool. Of the 2 local stories available, 1 aired, and the roundup did not open with local news. Local material reached the episode through the deep dive, where the lead is Cariboo and the single source is My Cariboo Now.

The deep-dive beat count is 4 aired against 5 planned, so the segment ran one beat short. Only 6 of 17 bridges were named, and no roundup pairs were placed in plan order. Treat the bridge gap as the likely cause of the missing beat and the unplaced pairs, and make bridge naming a required output of the script step.

Two released holds were older articles, and 32 on-theme candidates went unused

Focus routing released 2 held articles and held none. Both were held from earlier in the cycle: one from 2026-11-09 and one from 2026-11-12, both on kw=1. The tonight's focus is Sky & Cosmos, cycle week 1 of 5, but neither released article is a Sky & Cosmos piece, so the release came from the hold queue rather than from tonight's focus match.

Meanwhile 32 on-theme candidates were left unused. Those are the pool's remaining material after the cut, not a shortage. The routing is working, but the release rule is letting older held items through ahead of fresher on-theme ones. Review the release ordering in focus routing.

items.title: [100 Mile Free Press] Clinton and District Comunity Forests of BC Ltd. – Forest Operation Maps, Invitation to Comment
items.content_html: The public is invited to review and comment on the Clinton and District Community Forests of BC Ltd’s Forest Operations Maps (FOM). The FOM shows proposed road construction and cut block development under the listed Forest Stewardship Plan (FSP) within Forest Development Units in the 100 Mile House Natural Resource District (DMH). This FOM has a validity period of 3 years beginning March 2, 2026. During the validity period the Clinton and District Community Forest of BC Ltd may apply for Cutting Permits containing cut blocks and apply for road permits to construct roads shown on their FOM.

Focus: Governance, Title & Treaty (week 1 of 4). Run 43180110799.

▲
Shipped, needs a look1 thing to look at before tomorrow's run.

What to do

  1. script/pronunciation fell back. Search the run log for Degraded 'script/pronunciation' and decide whether the fallback is acceptable or the cause needs fixing.
    degrade() row: 1 name(s) with no entry in config/pronunciations.json: Esk'et

What happened

The deep dive fell to one story and the roundup dropped 19 candidates

The episode ran one deep dive, a single story from My Cariboo Now on the Esk'etemc First Nation election this weekend. The debate question built on it asks whether the council and services decisions should be governed by a clear, transparent rule set that reflects both resident costs and member rights, given a narrow ten-vote election margin and low turnout. Casey carried 49% of the deep dive's words, and the voice ratio of Casey to Riley came in at 0.96.

The roundup dropped 19 stories from the pool because the airtime budget for NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT could not hold them. That is by design: the pool is larger than one segment can air, and a cut story can come back on a day when it fits better. The roundup citations matched 15 of 18, and the single deep-dive citation matched. Nothing about this run required a change to the budget.

The script came in under target and shipped at 3357 words

The first draft was 2608 words against a 3400-word target, so it went back for one expand pass. The shipped script is 3357 words, short of target but within the range the pipeline accepts. A thin day shipping under target is intended, and the pipeline only treats it as a problem under SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS.

The expand pass therefore brought the draft most of the way to target without reaching it. Anyone tuning the expand prompt should weigh that gap against the 2608-word first draft, not against the 3400 target alone.

One name had no pronunciation entry and went to TTS unmapped

The script step reported one name with no entry in config/pronunciations.json: Esk'et. The pipeline did not stop or substitute a fallback spelling; the name went to text-to-speech as written. Two TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicted, and one of those two retries stayed short. The longer take was kept, so no segment was dropped from the episode.

Add "Esk'et" to config/pronunciations.json before the next episode that names the nation, since this election will keep the name in rotation.
